note: The remake's data. Every drawn date has two sources or more, keyed to sources{}. Every number printed in the picture is formatted from this file: a label's template carries {lo}, {hi}, {at} or {age} and no digits of its own (make2.py refuses one that does). 'lo'/'hi' bound an uncertain date and are drawn as a fade or a block.

sources.SEP-M: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Marcus Aurelius' (plato.stanford.edu/entries/marcus-aurelius/), read 2026-11-17
sources.IEP-M: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Marcus Aurelius' (iep.utm.edu/marcus/), read 2026-11-17
sources.HA-M: Historia Augusta, Life of Marcus 1.5, 1.7, 2.6 and 3.1-3: Magie's Loeb translation and the Latin, both on LacusCurtius (penelope.uchicago.edu), read 2026-11-17
sources.MED-1.6: Meditations 1.6, Long's translation (classics.mit.edu): from Diognetus, devotion to philosophy and the wish for a plank bed and skin; undated; read 2026-11-17
sources.MED-1.7: Meditations 1.7, Long's translation (classics.mit.edu): Rusticus made him 'acquainted with the discourses of Epictetus, which he communicated to me out of his own collection'; undated; read 2026-11-17
sources.WIKI-M: Wikipedia, 'Marcus Aurelius': 'In April 132, at the behest of Diognetus, Marcus took up the dress and habits of the philosopher' (footnoted to Birley); read 2026-11-17
sources.DIO-72: Cassius Dio 72.33-34 (Loeb epitome, LacusCurtius): died 17 March, emperor nineteen years and eleven days; read 2026-11-17

notes.label: a student, Arrian, writes down his lectures, c. {lo}–{hi}
src: IEP-E: the Discourses 'written some time around the years 104–107' (a conjecture)
SEP-E: the teaching the Discourses record dates 'around the year 108 by Millar's (1965) dating'
WIKI-E: Arrian 'studied under him as a young man, around 108 AD'
notes.doubt: No source dates the writing-down itself firmly: IEP's 104–107 is a conjecture, and SEP's 108 dates the teaching, with Arrian in the room. SEP also reports Dobbin's view that Epictetus may have written the texts himself.

cloak.label: at {age}, a philosopher's dress
src: HA-M 2.6, Latin (LacusCurtius, Hohl's text): 'nam duodecimum annum ingressus habitum philosophi sumpsit', having entered his twelfth year, he took up the dress of a philosopher; Magie's English renders it 'when he was twelve years old'
WIKI-M 'In April 132 ... took up the dress and habits of the philosopher' (Birley)
MED-1.6 the plank bed and skin, undated
cloak.doubt: Entering his twelfth year, from a birth in April 121, is April 132 to April 133, age eleven; Birley's April 132 agrees. Magie's translation says 'twelve', which I first followed. The Historia Augusta is a late and often unreliable source; Meditations 1.6 supports the boyhood discipline but gives no age. Drawn grey, not red: one late life is not a hinge.

label: notes of his lectures,
lent to Marcus by Rusticus;
the year is not recorded
src: MED-1.7

SEP-M: 'In i.7, Marcus speaks of reading Epictetus' 'hupomnêmata'; Arrian, who wrote down Epictetus' teachings, named them hupomnêmata, apparently in reference to Xenophon's Memorabilia (Greek title: 'hupomnêmata') of Socrates.'
paper.doubt: SEP says Arrian named his record hupomnêmata, the word Marcus uses in 1.7. That makes it likely, not certain, that Rusticus's copy was Arrian's record. I did not read the Greek of Arrian's preface myself.
